topics.title: What Is a Force?
topics.keyConcept: A force is a push or pull resulting from an interaction between objects.

topics.title: What Can a Force Do to the Objects on Which It Is Applied?
topics.keyConcept: Force can change an object's motion, speed, direction, or shape.

topics.title: Are Forces an Interaction Between Two or More Objects?
topics.keyConcept: Forces arise through interactions between objects.

topics.title: Contact Forces
topics.keyConcept: Contact forces require physical contact between interacting objects.

topics.title: Friction
topics.keyConcept: Friction is a contact force that opposes motion between surfaces in contact.

topics.title: Non-contact Forces
topics.keyConcept: Some forces act at a distance without physical contact.

topics.title: Magnetic Force
topics.keyConcept: Magnets exert forces of attraction or repulsion without direct contact.

topics.title: Electrostatic Force
topics.keyConcept: Charged objects can attract or repel through electrostatic force.

topics.title: Gravitational Force
topics.keyConcept: Gravity is the attractive force with which Earth pulls objects toward itself.

topics.title: Weight and Its Measurement
topics.keyConcept: Weight is gravitational force and is measured in newtons using instruments such as a spring balance.

topics.title: Floating and Sinking
topics.keyConcept: Buoyant force and gravity determine whether an object floats or sinks in a liquid.

topics.title: Financial Statements
topics.keyConcept: Prepare trading and profit and loss accounts and a balance sheet for a sole proprietorship, including prescribed adjustments.

topics.title: Incomplete Records
topics.keyConcept: Ascertain profit or loss using the statement of affairs method for incomplete records.
